name: td1_failing_test
stressor: test-driven fix + error recovery: a shipped unittest suite has ONE failing test pinning correct behavior plus several passing tests; the fix must turn the failing test green without regressing any passing one. The bug is a real logic defect (leftover pennies dumped on the last share instead of largest-remainder distribution) that conserves the total, so the easy 'sum is preserved' tests stay green and mask it.
source_note: Purpose-built integer-cents expense-splitting library authored for this benchmark: money.py (parse/format/round-half-up), allocator.py (proportional penny allocation), ledger.py (Expense/Ledger built on allocator), and a unittest suite test_split.py. setup() corrupts exactly one tail line of allocator.allocate() so leftover cents pile onto the last share ('shares[-1] += leftover') instead of the largest-remainder distribution; the failing test test_leftover_pennies_are_fair pins the correct split, while money/ledger/conservation tests pass. reference_fix reverts that one line. The oracle re-runs the WHOLE suite in a fresh `python -B -m unittest` subprocess (must be all green) AND, in a second fresh child, hammers allocate() with uneven/weighted totals the agent never saw, checking exact largest-remainder results plus invariants (sum preserved, off-by-<=1 from floor, validation intact).
discriminator: The agent must satisfy a CONJUNCTION of constraints that live in different tests: the one failing fairness test AND every passing test (money rounding, allocator conservation, allocator validation, ledger zero-sum) AND unseen oracle assertions. A bounded-slice agent re-reads allocator.py and the whole test file each turn, so it sees that 'sum preserved' already holds and the only missing constraint is the distribution rule, and edits the single tail line. A growing-transcript agent that read the failing test early and then iterated tends to lose the other tests' constraints (e.g. reaching for a quick hard-code of [34,33,33] / the 101-case, or rewriting allocate in a way that drops the AllocationError validation or breaks an even split) and regresses a passing test or fails the unseen inputs -- the error-recovery loop must hold ALL constraints live at once, which is exactly what truncation/transcript-bloat erodes.
